notYet: Not yet part of Carthage and Numidia

stages.name: Carthaginian
stages.desc: Held by Carthage or its armies

stages.name: Syphax's Masaesyli
stages.desc: The upper hand lies with Syphax, king of western Numidia

stages.name: Masinissa's Massyli
stages.desc: The upper hand lies with Gala's son Masinissa, of eastern Numidia

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The Maurusii of the Atlantic coast, facing Gades across the strait, stay out of the war
The beaten Syphax takes refuge among the Maurusii and raises a new force
The Moorish king Baga gives Masinissa an escort of four thousand to ride home

states.name: Spain
timeline: Carthage holds the south and east, its silver and its recruits; Rome holds a foothold north of the Ebro
Both elder Scipios die in battle, with Masinissa's horsemen riding for Carthage
Publius Scipio storms New Carthage, the Carthaginian base in Spain
After Ilipa and the surrender of Gades, Carthage is finished in Spain

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage's African heartland: the city and the farmland of the Bagradas valley
Laelius raids the coast for Rome, and Masinissa's refuge is near the Lesser Syrtis
Scipio lands near Utica but cannot take it, and winters on a coastal headland
After the burned camps and the Great Plains, Scipio holds Tunis and the Bagradas valley
Hannibal is beaten at Zama, and Carthage asks for terms
The treaty leaves Carthage its African lands, but almost no fleet and no free hand in war

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Syphax of the Masaesyli is the strongest king here, allied to Rome; Gala's Massyli hold the east
Masinissa, Gala's son, routs Syphax and drives him to the Atlantic coast
Masinissa leaves for Spain and Syphax recovers his kingdom; the date is approximate
Gala dies, the Massyli fight over his throne, and Syphax takes Massyli land
Masinissa regains a foothold between Cirta and Hippo, but Syphax drives him out again
Syphax marries Hasdrubal's daughter and swears alliance with Carthage
Syphax is captured and Cirta opens its gates to Masinissa; Syphax's son Vermina still holds the far west
The peace confirms Masinissa's kingdom under Rome's protection

events.title: Centurions reach Syphax
events.text: The Scipio brothers send Syphax three centurions; one, Statorius, stays to train him an infantry on the Roman model.

events.title: Carthage courts Gala
events.text: Carthaginian envoys urge Gala, king of the Massyli, to strike before Syphax can join the Romans.

events.title: Masinissa routs Syphax
events.text: Gala's son, seventeen by Livy's count, wins a great battle; Livy's thirty thousand dead is a figure no one can check, and the site is unknown.

events.title: Syphax flees west
events.text: With a few horsemen Syphax reaches the Maurusii on the Atlantic coast, raises a new force, and is beaten again by Masinissa.

events.title: Publius Scipio falls
events.text: Masinissa's horsemen harry the Roman army in Spain until it is destroyed near Castulo and its commander killed.

events.title: Gnaeus Scipio falls
events.text: Weeks later the second Roman army is caught and destroyed near Ilorca, and Rome almost loses Spain.

events.title: A young commander lands
events.text: Publius Scipio, about twenty-five and son of the dead general, takes the Spanish command at Emporiae and Tarraco.

events.title: New Carthage falls
events.text: Scipio storms the Carthaginian base in Spain, seizing its treasury, its stores and its hostages.

events.title: Massiva sent home
events.text: After the battle of Baecula, Scipio frees a captured boy, Masinissa's nephew, and sends him home with gifts: a gesture Masinissa remembers.

events.title: Hasdrubal at Gades
events.text: Hasdrubal, son of Gisco, falls back toward Gades and raises a last great army for the defence of Spain.

events.title: Battle of Ilipa
events.text: Scipio destroys the last Carthaginian field army in Spain, though Masinissa's cavalry fights hard for Carthage.

events.title: Masinissa changes sides
events.text: From Gades he sends word to Scipio; they meet in secret with small escorts, and he promises help in Africa.

events.title: Dinner with Syphax
events.text: Scipio and Hasdrubal find themselves guests of Syphax and share a couch at his table; Scipio leaves with a treaty. Siga is the traditional setting.

events.title: Gades surrenders
events.text: Mago sails away and the old Phoenician city goes over to Rome, ending Carthage's rule in Spain.

events.title: Gala dies
events.text: The Massyli crown passes to Gala's brother, then to a cousin who is killed in a coup, and the kingdom falls into civil war.

events.title: Baga's escort
events.text: The Moorish king Baga lends Masinissa four thousand riders to take him home to claim the throne.

events.title: Laelius raids Hippo
events.text: Scipio's lieutenant plunders the coast near Hippo; Masinissa meets him and complains that Scipio is too slow.

events.title: Reported dead
events.text: Syphax's officer Bocchar hunts Masinissa to a river near Clupea; two companions drown, and Carthage hears he is dead.

events.title: Masinissa returns
events.text: Healed in a cave and back with forty riders, he raises his people and holds the heights between Cirta and Hippo.

events.title: Refuge at the Syrtis
events.text: Beaten again by Syphax and his son Vermina, Masinissa withdraws with a handful of riders to the Lesser Syrtis.

events.title: Scipio in Sicily
events.text: Consul at about thirty, Scipio trains the army of Sicily, including survivors of Cannae, for the crossing to Africa.

events.title: Hasdrubal's daughter married
events.text: Hasdrubal sends to Carthage for his daughter and hurries a wedding that binds Syphax to Carthage by oath. Appian says she had first been promised to Masinissa.

events.title: Syphax warns Scipio
events.text: His envoys reach Sicily: if Rome invades, he must fight for his homeland and his wife's city.

events.title: The fleet sails
events.text: Scipio's fleet leaves Lilybaeum for Africa with the prayers of the crowd on the shore.

events.title: Fair Promontory
events.text: Scipio lands at a headland near Utica and takes its name as an omen; Coelius, says Livy, told of a storm-wrecked crossing instead.

events.title: Trap at Salaeca
events.text: Masinissa, now with Scipio, lures Carthage's cavalry into an ambush; its commander Hanno is killed.

events.title: Utica holds
events.text: After forty days of siege, the armies of Syphax and Hasdrubal force Scipio off, and he winters on a nearby headland.

events.title: The camps burn
events.text: Scipio breaks off peace talks and attacks by night; Livy counts forty thousand dead, Polybius only thousands upon thousands.

events.title: The Great Plains
events.text: Syphax and Hasdrubal fight again with four thousand Celtiberians, who stand and die when the line breaks.

events.title: Tunis occupied
events.text: Scipio camps in sight of Carthage, and the city recalls Hannibal from Italy.

events.title: Syphax captured
events.text: Pursued by Laelius and Masinissa, Syphax loses his horse in battle and is taken alive.

events.title: Cirta opens
events.text: The city's leaders refuse threats, then open the gates when they see their king in chains.

events.title: Poison at Cirta
events.text: Sophonisba dies by poison. Livy has Masinissa send a slave with the cup; Appian has him hand it to her himself.

events.title: Scipio crowns Masinissa
events.text: A day later Scipio hails him as king before the army and gives him a golden crown and triumphal regalia, says Livy.

events.title: Hannibal lands
events.text: Hannibal comes ashore near Leptis Minor and spends the winter gathering an army around Hadrumetum.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.text: Masinissa brings six thousand foot and four thousand horse, and his cavalry helps break Hannibal's army; the site remains disputed.

events.title: Vermina beaten
events.text: Syphax's son, marching too late to help Carthage, is destroyed by Roman forces in December.

events.title: Hasdrubal's end
events.text: Appian says a mob accuses him of treason; he takes poison in his father's tomb, and his head is paraded through Carthage.

events.title: Peace with Rome
events.text: Carthage keeps its African lands but gives up all but ten warships, pays ten thousand talents, and may not wage war without Rome's leave.

events.title: Masinissa, king of Numidia
events.text: Rome confirms his rule from Cirta over the old Massyli lands and much of Syphax's kingdom. He reigns until 148 BC.

events.title: Syphax dies
events.text: Livy says he died at Tibur shortly before the triumph; Polybius says he walked in it.

events.title: Scipio's triumph
events.text: Scipio returns to Rome in splendour and is remembered as Africanus, the first general named for the land he conquered.

eras: The War of the Numidian Kings
chartNote: Share of the area of four present-day countries, each coloured by the power dominant across most of it. This is a simplification: regions are today's boundaries, Algeria's Saharan south counts though no king ruled it, and Algeria held both Numidian kingdoms at once, so its colour follows whichever king had the upper hand. Dates and figures rest on Greek and Roman writers who often disagree.
